subject: Hosted API - regional custody & timed erasure clarifications
messages:
From: Heliotrope Health Security <security@heliotrope.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Heliotrope Procurement <procurement@heliotrope.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on where customer data lives and deletion proof (hosted API)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a short list of clarifications before we move to an internal sign-off:

1) For the hosted API, where are customer request/response payloads persisted? Which specific regions and cloud providers hold the payloads for a US tenant?
2) What is the default time-to-live for stored payloads and embeddings used for model context / caching? Can we configure or shorten this TTL?
3) When a customer requests deletion, what is the timeline and what artifacts are removed (backups, logs, cache copies, model KV)?
4) Do deletion events emit a verifiable audit trail (timestamped, tenant-id, actor) that we can accept as evidence?
5) What is your retention policy for system logs that might contain identifying strings?

We'd appreciate a short written response and a sample deletion audit CSV for a test tenant if possible.

Best,
Sara Khan
Information Security
Heliotrope Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Heliotrope Health Security <security@heliotrope.com>
Cc: Heliotrope Procurement <procurement@heliotrope.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data lives and deletion proof (hosted API)

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Lauren from Product Ops is cc'ed and will follow with the deletion playbook and a sample audit export.

1) Regional custody: For US tenants we store request/response payloads in AWS us-west-2 or us-east-1 depending on customer preference/region selection. We can pin a tenant to a region during onboarding.

2) Default TTL: By default hosted API request/response payloads and ephemeral request caches are retained for 30 days to support debugging and support investigations. Embeddings stored for reranking/semantic search are retained per-customer policy but default to 90 days; both TTLs are configurable per-account with a minimum of 0 days (i.e., immediate expiry) for supported plans.

3) Deletion timeline: Typical flow —
- Deletion request accepted: start of pipeline (t0)
- Main tenant data removed from primary stores: within 24 hours
- KV/prefix caches invalidated (in-memory & disk-backed caches): within 48 hours; in-flight cache entries are purged and flagged
- Backups snapshot removal: within 30 days (we maintain a short backup window for disaster recovery; we provide accelerated retention removal for enterprise agreements)

4) Audit trail: Yes — deletion events generate an auditable record (tenant_id, action, initiator_email, timestamp, request_id). We can provide CSV exports and sign an attestation if needed. I've attached a sample deletion audit CSV and our SOC2 attestation.

5) Logs: System logs that may contain identifying strings are retained by default for 90 days. We mask PII in logs by default and offer configurable scrubbing and redaction rules. Longer retention windows are available behind SSO/KMS entitlements.

I've attached: SOC2-TypeII-Attestation.pdf and sample-deletion-audit-20270410.csv. Lauren will follow with the playbook and a few technical clarifications.

Would you like a short call (30 min) to walk through the audit CSV and attestation?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Heliotrope Health Security <security@heliotrope.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data lives and deletion proof (hosted API)

Hi Sara —

On behalf of Product Ops, adding more detail and the hosted API deletion playbook (attached). Key items below in plain terms so your auditors can map them to controls:

- Storage topology: Request/response payloads are written to encrypted object storage (AES-256) in the region selected during tenant provisioning. Metadata and tenant routing tables are in a separate encrypted DB within the same region to avoid cross-region metadata exposure.

- Encryption & keys: All at-rest encryption uses customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private; hosted API uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. We can enable CMEK for enterprise contracts; keys are not exported.

- Cache behavior: The serving runtime uses short-lived KV caches to accelerate autoregressive generation. Cache entries are ephemeral and tied to request_ids; we invalidate entries upon deletion and rotate cache namespaces nightly to prevent stale persistence. Cache invalidation is synchronous (best-effort) and asynchronous verification runs mark purged keys for removal from any eventual-disk storage.

- Backups & snapshots: Backups are incremental. When a deletion request is processed we mark the tenant as deleted and schedule snapshot compaction; explicit snapshot deletion jobs run in the next maintenance window — typically within 30 days. For customers requiring immediate snapshot purge we include an accelerated deletion clause in the contract.

- Audit evidence: The CSV sample Dylan attached contains the fields your team requested. Fields: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, actor, action_type, request_id, object_paths_affected. We also provide signed attestations for deletion events (PDF) and can push records to your SIEM via secure webhook for real-time observability.

- Log redaction: We support runtime PII scrubbing rules (regex-based and token-based) as part of our logging pipeline. For regulated customers we can enable deterministic hashing of any user identifiers before they leave the tenant boundary.

Attachment: hostedapi-deletion-playbook.pdf — includes canonical flow diagrams, SLAs, and the audit CSV schema.

If you need a tenant-specific experiment, we can run a deletion on a synthetic tenant and provide a notarized audit trail. Happy to coordinate scheduling.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Heliotrope Health Security <security@heliotrope.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Heliotrope Procurement <procurement@heliotrope.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data lives and deletion proof (hosted API)

Thanks Lauren and Dylan — that helps. A couple of follow-ups before we proceed to legal:

1) We'd like a one-off deletion run on a test tenant (tenant_id: heliotrope-demo-001) and a time-stamped signed attestation plus the raw audit CSV. Can you confirm you can provide a signed PDF attestation we can keep with our audit artifacts?
2) Our compliance team is concerned about the 30-day snapshot window. Can you confirm whether the snapshots contain decrypted payloads and the process for snapshot compaction?
3) For logs retained at 90 days, is there a way to scope those logs (e.g., exclude chat transcripts) so that we can limit PII exposure?

If you can provide the test-run evidence and the signed attestation, procurement is ready to start paperwork.

Best,
Sara Khan
Information Security
Heliotrope Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Heliotrope Health Security <security@heliotrope.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data lives and deletion proof (hosted API)

Sara —

We can run the heliotrope-demo-001 deletion this week and provide: 1) raw audit CSV, 2) a signed attestation PDF, and 3) verification screenshots from the deletion job pipeline. Action plan:
- Tue 2027-04-20 02:00 UTC: schedule deletion job in staging (will not touch production)
- Wed 2027-04-21 09:00 UTC: export audit CSV and generate attestation (signed by Head of Security Ops)
- Wed 2027-04-21 12:00 UTC: share artifacts via secure Drive link and provide a temporary SIEM webhook for you to validate the events in real time

Answers inline:
- Snapshots: snapshots are encrypted at rest and do not contain plaintext outside the storage service; snapshot compaction removes blocks referencing deleted objects; the compaction job is irreversible once complete. We can offer an accelerated compaction/expunge for your org as a contract term if that is required.
- Log scoping: yes — we can configure the logging pipeline to exclude chat transcript payloads or selectively redact fields before they are indexed. We'll include the logging scope configuration in the runbook we provide.

Next steps: Dylan/Procurement — confirm the signing authority for the attestation and we'll lock the test-time. Lauren — I'll coordinate the staging job.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security Operations
Redwood Inference
